questions.question: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged? 14014 × 14 − 10 ÷ 8 + 14 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?
14014 × 14 − 10 ÷ 8 + 14 = ?
questions.solution:
According to the question, after '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged:

14014 × 14 − 10 ÷ 8 + 14 = ? ⇒ 14014 ÷ 14 + 10 × 8 - 14 = ?

⇒ 14014 ÷ 14 + 10 × 8 - 14 = ? ⇒ 1001 + 10 × 8 - 14 = ?⇒ 1001 + 80 - 14 = ? ⇒ 1081 - 14 = ? ⇒ 1067 = ?

questions.question: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 48 ÷ 3 + 12 × 4 – 6 × 7 + 21 = 27
questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?
48 ÷ 3 + 12 × 4 – 6 × 7 + 21 = 27
questions.solution:
Option 1) 3 and 4

48 ÷ 3 + 12 × 4 – 6 × 7 + 21 = 27 ⇒ 48 ÷ 4 + 12 × 3 – 6 × 7 + 21 = 27

⇒ 48 ÷ 4 + 12 × 3 – 6 × 7 + 21 = 27 ⇒ 12 + 12 × 3 – 6 × 7 + 21 = 27 ⇒ 12 + 36 + 21 – 42 = 27 ⇒ 69 – 42 = 27 ⇒ 27 = 27 (LHS = RHS)

questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bottles are jugs. Some bottles are flasks. All flasks are bins. Conclusions: I. Some bottles are bins. II. Some jugs are bins. III. Some flasks are jugs.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if
they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the
statements.
Statements:
All bottles are jugs.
Some bottles are flasks.
All flasks are bins.
Conclusions:
I. Some bottles are bins.
II. Some jugs are bins.
III. Some flasks are jugs.

options.text: All conclusions I, II and III follow
options.html: All conclusions I, II and III follow

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.html: Either conclusion I or II follows

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some bottles are bins → Follow (As some bottles are flasks and all flasks are bins. As bottles has some part common with flasks which whole comes in bins, therefore it is true.)

II. Some jugs are bins → Follow (As all bottles are jugs, some bottles are flasks and all flasks are bins. As whole bottles comes in jugs and has some part common with flasks which whole comes in bins, therefore it is true.)

III. Some flasks are jugs → Follow (As all bottles are jugs and some bottles are flasks. As whole bottles comes in jugs and has some part common with flasks, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, All conclusions I, II and III follow.
